newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian shares slide in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian shares slide in dull trade.

text.p: Lithuanian shares slid in dull trade on Tuesday, leaving dealers in a bearish mood.
"Prices should stop falling at the end of this week or the start of next week, but they probably won't rise very much for a while," said one dealer.
Dealers said that the market seemed still to be in the process of correcting itself after January's brief bull run, when prices surged to new highs.
"January's price increases were speculative and not really based on the activities of the companies concerned," said Robertas Berzinskas of Vilniaus Bank's brokerage house.
"A number of shares still seem to be overpriced," he said.
Dealers also said that market activity was being kept to a minimum while investors waited for first quarter results from a number of key companies.
Another factor cited by dealers is the general situation across Eastern Europe, where share prices have declined in recent days.
But Warsaw offered some hope to Lithuanian market players, rebounding on Tuesday after a three-session fall.
Lithuania's blue chip losses were across the board, hitting companies from the energy to the banking sector.

Lithuanian Gas returned to the market after being suspended from trade for several days for a shareholders' meeting that never was and promptly lost ten percent, falling to 1.98 litas from 2.20 litas.
The company's shareholders' meeting, originally scheduled for Monday, was postponed for two weeks because of a dispute with the auditors over legal documents.
Officials from the state-run firm also confirmed that its 1996 losses may exceed 78 million litas.
Hermis Bank fell to 190.00 litas from 195.00 litas in trade of 24,320 litas, while Vilniaus Bank remained unchanged at 245.00 litas in trade of over 56,000 litas.
